info.title: WeFlow command API contract
info.description: The types of the answers of the command API that the WeFlow WebUI reads (#399); `/openapi.json` of `weflow serve` describes every route. Generated by a test of weflow-cli, see docs/serve-api.md.

data.description: The usernames left out of the analytics, as saved
The official accounts followed: the rows of WeChat's contact table, each with `lastTime`, the time of its conversation's last message (null without one)
What was removed; with `dry-run`, what would be
What was removed; with `dry-run`, what would be
With `parsed=true`, the contacts as the desktop app lists them; else the rows of WeChat's table
Each conversation asked for, with how many messages it has
The conversation's details; with `fast`, only its facts; with `extra` alone, only where its messages are kept
With `parsed=true`, the message as the chat window shows it; else its row and the message as the query commands list it
With `parsed=true`, the messages as the chat window shows them; else the rows of WeChat's table, each with its `_cursor`
With `parsed=true`, the hits, each with its `_session_id`, as the chat window shows them; else the rows of WeChat's table, each with its `_cursor`
Each username asked for, with whether its conversation is folded and muted
The file written; with several formats or `zip`, the folder or zip and each format's file
How many posts each poster has, by username; with `user`, that one's

anyOf.description: Each poster, with how many posts they have

data.description: The versions downloaded; with `remote`, the ones published

username.description: The other party's wxid, `…@chatroom` for a group, `gh_…` for an official account.

type.description: WeChat's type of the conversation's row; 0 for an official account WeChat lists without one.

summary.description: The last message as the list shows it.

sortTimestamp.description: What the list is ordered by; 0 for an official account WeChat lists without a conversation.

lastMsgType.description: WeChat's type of the last message, as a message's `localType`.

messageCountHint.description: About how many messages the conversation has, when WeChat's row or its tables say.

displayName.description: The remark, else the nickname, else the username.

lastMsgSender.description: In a group: who sent the last message.

Session.description: A conversation of `chat sessions`, newest first.

localId.description: The message's id in its conversation's table; with `createTime`, the key of `chat message`.

serverId.description: WeChat's id of the message, in decimal: a string, as it may pass 2^53.

localType.description: WeChat's type of the message (1 text, 3 image, 34 voice, 43 video, 47 sticker, 49 app message, 10000 system…).

sortSeq.description: WeChat's order of the messages of a conversation: the send time in milliseconds, plus a little.

isSend.description: 1 when I sent it, 0 when I received it; null when the row does not say.

senderUsername.description: Who sent it; null when the row does not say.

parsedContent.description: The text the chat window shows.

rawContent.description: The message as WeChat keeps it (often XML).

messageKey.description: The message's key: the same message has the same key on every machine. It is opaque; only compare it.

_cursor.description:
Where the message stands in its conversation: pass it as `before` or `after` to read the messages next to it.
It is opaque; only the server reads it.

_session_id.description: The conversation of a search hit.

ParsedMessage.description:
A message of a page as the chat window shows it (`chat messages`, `chat message` and `chat search` with
`parsed`).

message.description: Null when the row could not be read as a message.

MessageLookup.description: `chat message` without `parsed`: the row of WeChat's table, and the message as the query commands list it.

serverId.description: WeChat's id of the message, in decimal: a string, as it may pass 2^53.

localType.description: WeChat's type of the message, as a parsed message's `localType`.

content.description: The message as WeChat keeps it (often XML).

text.description: Its text as the chat window shows it; null when it has none.

appMsgKind.description: The kind of an app message (`link`, `file`, `music`…).

MessageView.description:
A message as the query commands list it (`chat resources`, `chat images`, `chat media-stream`…): the main fields
of its row, its text and the keys of its media. An optional field is left out when the message has none.

displayName.description: The remark, else the nickname, else the WeChat ID, else the username.

labels.description: The names of the contact's labels.

Contact.description:
A contact of `chat contacts --parsed`, as the desktop app lists it: the most recent conversation first, then by
name. A text field is left out when it is empty.

ContactKind.description: What a contact of `chat contacts --parsed` is.

nextCursor.description: The `_cursor` of the last item, to pass as `before` for the next page; null on the last page.

serverId.description: WeChat's id of the message, in decimal: a string, as it may pass 2^53.

localType.description: WeChat's type of the message, as a parsed message's `localType`.

content.description: The message as WeChat keeps it (often XML).

text.description: Its text as the chat window shows it; null when it has none.

appMsgKind.description: The kind of an app message (`link`, `file`, `music`…).

_cursor.description: Where the message stands in the listing (not in its conversation): `before` reads on from it.

Resource.description: A message of `chat resources`, newest first.

ResourceKind.description: What a message of `chat resources` holds.

ChatStatus.description: Whether a conversation is folded and muted, of `chat statuses`, which answers one for each username asked for.

TabCounts.description: How many contacts of each kind there are (`chat tab-counts`), as the tabs of the desktop app count them.

SessionDates.description: The days a conversation has messages on (`chat dates`), as `YYYY-MM-DD` in the server's time zone, oldest first.

SessionDateCounts.description: How many messages a conversation has on each day it has any (`chat date-counts`), by `YYYY-MM-DD`.

displayName.description: The remark, else the nickname, else the alias, else the username.

firstMessageTime.description: The time of its first message; null when its tables do not say.

SessionDetail.description: A conversation's details (`chat detail`): its facts, and where its messages are kept.

dbName.description: The database's file name, such as `message_0.db`.

MessageTable.description: One of WeChat's tables that holds messages of a conversation.

displayName.description: The remark, else the nickname, else the alias, else the username.

SessionFacts.description: Who a conversation is with and how many messages it has (`chat detail --fast`).

firstMessageTime.description: The time of its first message; null when its tables do not say.

SessionTables.description: Where a conversation's messages are kept (`chat detail --extra`, and `chat detail` without `fast`).

normal.description: The image shown when it is opened.

hd.description: The original, once View original downloaded it.

normalBytes.description: Bytes of the image; null when neither the message nor its file says.

hdBytes.description: Bytes of the original, as the message gives them even before it is downloaded.

ImageInfo.description: Which files of a message's image are on this computer (`chat image-info`), and the sizes the message gives.

GroupChat.description: A group chat of `group list`, the largest first.

fromCache.description: Whether the panel was kept from a request a short while before (`refresh=true` builds it again).

updatedAt.description: When the panel was built, in Unix milliseconds.

GroupMembers.description:
The members of a group (`group members`), as the members panel of the desktop app lists them: the owner first,
then friends, then by how many messages they sent.

displayName.description: Their name as WeChat shows it in the group.

nickname.description: The fields of their contact; empty when they are not a contact.

groupNickname.description: The name they gave themselves in this group; empty when none.

messageCount.description: How many messages they sent in the group; 0 unless `counts=true`.

GroupMember.description: A member of a group's members panel.

GroupRank.description: Who sent how many messages in a group (`group ranking`), the most first.

hourlyDistribution.description: By the hour, `"0"` to `"23"`, in the server's time zone.

GroupHours.description: How many messages a group has in each hour of the day (`group hours`).

GroupMedia.description: How many messages of each kind a group has (`group media`), the most first.

type.description: WeChat's type of the message, as `localType`; -1 for all the others together.

name.description: Its name as the desktop app shows it, in Chinese.

MediaCount.description: One kind of message and how many there are.

timeDistribution.description: By the hour, `"0"` to `"23"`, in the server's time zone.

commonPhrases.description: What they said most, the most first, up to 10.

MemberAnalytics.description: What one member of a group sent (`group member`).

receivedMessages.description: Always 0: a member's messages are all sent by them.

firstMessageTime.description: The time of their first message; null when they sent none.

messageTypeCounts.description: By WeChat's type of the message, as `localType`.

MemberStatistics.description: The numbers of a member's messages.

PhraseCount.description: A phrase and how often it was said.

EmojiCount.description: An emoji and how often it was sent.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` for the next page.

MemberMessages.description: A page of a member's messages in a group (`group member-messages`), newest first.

localId.description: The message's id in its conversation's table; with `createTime`, the key of `chat message`.

serverId.description: WeChat's id of the message, in decimal: a string, as it may pass 2^53.

localType.description: WeChat's type of the message (1 text, 3 image, 34 voice, 43 video, 47 sticker, 49 app message, 10000 system…).

sortSeq.description: WeChat's order of the messages of a conversation: the send time in milliseconds, plus a little.

isSend.description: 1 when I sent it, 0 when I received it; null when the row does not say.

senderUsername.description: Who sent it; null when the row does not say.

parsedContent.description: The text the chat window shows.

rawContent.description: The message as WeChat keeps it (often XML).

messageKey.description: The message's key: the same message has the same key on every machine. It is opaque; only compare it.

ChatMessage.description:
A message as the chat window shows it (`chat messages --parsed` and the other parsed reads, #399): its text and the
keys of its media, links, cards and so on, parsed from the row. An optional field is left out when the message has
none; times are Unix seconds.

firstMessageTime.description: The time of the first message; null without messages.

messageTypeCounts.description: By WeChat's type of the message, as `localType`.

OverallStatistics.description: The private chats counted together (`analytics overall`), but for the people left out.

wechatId.description: The WeChat ID they chose, else the username when it is not a `wxid_…`; else empty.

lastMessageTime.description: The time of the last message; null without messages.

ContactRank.description: A private chat of `analytics rankings`, the one with the most messages first.

weekdayDistribution.description: By the day of the week, `"1"` (Monday) to `"7"` (Sunday).

TimeDistribution.description: When the private chats' messages were sent (`analytics time`), in the server's time zone.

ExcludeCandidate.description:
Someone who may be left out of the analytics (`analytics exclude-candidates`): the private chats, and those left
out already.

SnsTimeline.description: A page of Moments posts (`sns timeline`), the newest first.

tid.description: The row's id in WeChat's table, in decimal.

nickname.description: The poster's name: the post's own, else the contact's, else the username.

type.description: WeChat's type of the post: 1 pictures, 15 a video, others links and such.

rawXml.description: The post's XML as WeChat keeps it.

likes.description: The names of those who liked it.

videoKey.description: The key of the post's video, which opens its cover too.

rawUrl.description:
With `with-media`: the server's addresses, `url` and `thumb` being those of the files it fetched, and where
it fetched them or a proxy of the server serves them.

livePhoto.description: The moving part of a live photo.

SnsMedia.description: A picture or video of a post: addresses on WeChat's servers, fetched and decrypted by `sns media` with `key`.

rawUrl.description: With `with-media`: as for the picture it moves.

SnsLivePhoto.description: The video of a live photo.

refCommentId.description: The comment it answers; empty when none.

SnsLocation.description: Where a post was made, as much as it says.

SnsUsers.description: Who has posts in Moments (`sns users`), the one who posted last first.

myPosts.description: How many of them are the account's own; null when the account's wxid is not known.

SnsStats.description: How many Moments posts there are (`sns stats`).

UserPosts.description: How many Moments posts one person has (`sns post-counts --user`).

strategy.description:
How they were found: `native` (WeChat's own index), `table-scan` (the time span of each table) or
`edge-scan` (each chat's first and last message).

ReportYears.description: The years with private messages (`report annual years`), the latest first.

coreFriends.description: The three private chats with the most messages.

topPhrases.description: My phrases said at least twice, the most said first.

AnnualReport.description: The annual report (`report annual generate`) over the private chats of one year, or of all of them.

CoreFriend.description: One of the three private chats with the most messages.

displayName.description: 「暂无」 for a month without messages.

MonthlyTopFriend.description: Who a month's most messages are with.

PeakDay.description: The day with the most messages, and who most of them are with.

LongestStreak.description: The most days in a row talked with one friend.

data.description: Seven rows, Monday first, of 24 hours each.

percentage.description: Of all the messages between 0:00 and 6:00, to one decimal.

MidnightKing.description: Who the most messages between 0:00 and 6:00 are with.

MutualFriend.description: The friend whose sent and received messages, 50 or more each, are closest to even.

initiativeRate.description: The share opened by me, in percent to one decimal.

topInitiatedFriend.description: Whom I opened the most conversations with; left out when I opened none.

SocialInitiative.description: Conversations opened by me or by them.

ResponseSpeed.description: How fast I answer, in seconds.

typeCounts.description: My posts by WeChat's post type.

topLikers.description: Who liked my posts the most.

topLiked.description: Whose posts I liked the most.

AnnualSnsStats.description: My Moments in the annual report.

periodDesc.description: The earlier period, as the report says it: 「去年的这个时候」 and the like.

LostFriend.description: A friend talked to much more in an earlier period than later.

firstChat.description: The first message ever between the two.

firstChatMessages.description: The first messages ever between the two, at most 10.

yearFirstChat.description: The first message of the year; null for all the years.

topPhrases.description: Phrases said at least twice by either, the most said first.

myExclusivePhrases.description: Phrases three quarters or more of which are mine.

friendExclusivePhrases.description: Phrases three quarters or more of which are the friend's.

heatmap.description: Seven rows, Monday first, of 24 hours each.

DualReport.description: The dual report (`report dual generate`): me and one friend, over one year or all of them.

content.description: Its text; raw for anything but text.

senderUsername.description: Who sent it; only on `firstChat`, where the row says.

DualMessage.description: A message of the dual report.

firstThreeMessages.description: The year's first messages, at most 10.

YearFirstChat.description: The first message of the year, with the first messages that follow it.

totalWords.description: The characters of the text messages.

DualStats.description: The counts of the dual report, and each one's most sent sticker.

DualInitiative.description: Conversations opened by me, or by them.

DualResponse.description: How fast I answer the friend, in seconds.

DualStreak.description: The most days in a row the two talked.

BizMessages.description: The pushes of an official account (`biz messages`), as the desktop app lists them.

localId.description: The message's id in its table; null when its row does not say.

contentList.description: The other articles of the push.

BizMessage.description: One push of an official account: its lead article and the others sent with it.

BizArticle.description: An article sent with a push.

hasMore.description:
Whether the WeChat Pay account has messages past this page; a page may hold fewer notices than `limit`, as
its other messages are left out.

PayRecords.description: A page of WeChat Pay notices (`biz pay-records`), newest first.

description.description: Its lines, as WeChat writes them (amount, method, state…).

merchantName.description: Who was paid; `WeChat Pay` (in the server's language) when the notice does not say.

timestamp.description: When it was published, in Unix seconds; 0 when the notice does not say.

decryptKey.description: Whether the database key is set.

imageKeys.description: Whether both image keys are set.

aiKey.description: Whether the key of the AI model API is set.

complete.description: Whether it can open the databases: the data directory and the database key are set.

ProfileSummary.description: A profile of the configuration (`config profiles`): its account and how far it is set up, without its keys.

target.description: The target it was built for, such as `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`.

RuntimeInfo.description: Where `weflow` keeps its files and what it is (`runtime info`).

part.description: Its name, as `cache clear` takes it.

CacheUsage.description: One part of WeFlow's cache (`cache list`), and how much of the disk it takes.

CachePart.description: A part of WeFlow's cache that is listed and cleared on its own.

bytes.description: What they all take on disk.

profileKeys.description: The profile keys it would unset (`clear-account`).

RemovalPlan.description: What `cache clear` or `clear-account` would remove (`--dry-run`), for a page that asks first.

PlannedRemoval.description: A file or folder a removal would take.

Cancelled.description: A removal the terminal was asked to confirm and was not.

freedBytes.description: What the removed files took on disk.

warnings.description: What could not be removed, and why; left out when everything was.

profileReset.description: Whether the account was taken out of the profile (`db_path`, `wxid`, the keys).

warnings.description: What could not be removed, and why; left out when everything was.

configPath.description: Null when `config unset config_path` finds no default place for it.

ConfigWritten.description: The config file a `config` change was written to.

skippedEncryptedKeys.description: The keys left out because the desktop app keeps them encrypted.

ConfigImported.description: What `config import` took from the desktop app's config.

lang.description: Output language chosen with `weflow lang en|zh` (`None` = follow the system).

ffmpeg_base_url.description: Mirror of the ffmpeg-static releases `weflow ffmpeg install` downloads from (`None` = GitHub).

ConfigStore.description: WeFlow's config file (`config list`): the profiles and the settings shared by all of them.

ProfileConfig.description: One profile of the config file: an account and its settings.

format.description: The format it was written in: `json`, `csv`, `excel`, …

ExportWritten.description: The file an export wrote (`export sessions`, `contacts`, `footprint`).

count.description: The members, or the messages, written.

filePath.description: Empty when no post matched, and nothing was written.

mediaCount.description: The media files copied beside it.

out.description: The file; in a zip of several formats, its name inside the zip.

media.description: The media copied beside it, with `media`.

MessagesExported.description: A conversation's messages written in one format (`export messages`).

missing.description: The ones whose file is not on disk, or could not be read.

hint.description: What to do, with the dates of the first ones.

MediaCopied.description: The media an export of messages copied to its `media/` folder.

time.description: The message's local time; `?` without one.

MissingImage.description: An image left out for lack of ffmpeg: where to find it in WeChat.

MessagesBundle.description: One conversation in several formats (`export messages` with several `format`s), or packed (`zip`).

MessagesFolder.description: The formats of one conversation, each written to its file in one folder.

files.description: Each format's file, named as it is inside the zip.

media.description: The media packed with them; null without `media`.

MessagesZip.description: The formats of one conversation packed into a zip, with their media.

thumbOnly.description: The exported images that are only the thumbnail.

hint.description: What to do, with the dates of the first ones.

isThumb.description: An image's: the file is only its thumbnail.
The file is only the thumbnail: the original is not on disk.

hasUpdate.description: A thumbnail whose original has since been downloaded.

ImageResult.description: Where a message's image is decrypted (`image decrypt`, `resolve-cache`); a failure says why instead.

success.description: Always true; each row says how it went.

ImageBatch.description: What `image resolve-batch` answers: one result per payload, in their order.

AutoDownloadStopped.description: What `image auto-download start` answers once stopped (Ctrl+C).

supported.description: Whether this computer can download WeChat's images on its own.

AutoDownloadStatus.description: What `image auto-download status` answers: the hook the desktop app used is not part of WeFlow.

coverUrl.description: A `data:` URL, or a `file://` one with `file-url`.

VideoInfo.description:
Where a message's video and its poster are (`video info`); the fields left out, as the desktop app's
`VideoInfo`, when there is nothing.

VideoMd5.description: The MD5 a video message names (`video parse-md5`); null when its XML has none.

source.description: Where it was downloaded from; left out when nothing was.

removedReleases.description: The folders of other releases taken away.

used.description: The ffmpeg WXGF images will use: one on `PATH` or in `FFMPEG_PATH` comes first.

FfmpegFound.description: The ffmpeg WXGF images use, and where it was found.

FfmpegPath.description: What `ffmpeg path` answers: the ffmpeg in use, and the mirror `ffmpeg install` downloads from.

FfmpegBaseUrl.description: The mirror `ffmpeg set baseurl` / `unset baseurl` left.

RuntimeManifest.description: What the binary carries (`runtime manifest`): its version, target and built-in files.

AssetManifestEntry.description: A file built into the binary.

inUse.description: The version `serve` shows; null when none is downloaded.

builtIn.description: The version this weflow was built for.

WebInfo.description: What `web info` answers: the WebUI `serve` shows, and the versions downloaded.

WebInstalled.description: A downloaded WebUI version (`web list`, `web install`).

why.description: Why it does not suit; null when it does.

before.description: The version wanted before; null when there was none.

WebUpdated.description: The WebUI version `web update` moved to.

shown.description: Versions a running `serve` shows, kept until it stops.

DbScan.description: The accounts `db scan` found under a folder: those with a `db_storage` or `FileStorage/Image` folder.

decrypt_key.description: Left out with `save`: it went to the profile instead.

DbKey.description: The database key `key db` read from WeChat.

image_xor_key.description: Left out with `save`, as `image_aes_key`: they went to the profile instead.

verified.description: Both keys were checked: the AES key on an image header and the XOR key on a whole image.

sources.description: The `kvcomm` files the keys came from.

collection.description: What was read of the `kvcomm` folders.

scan.description: What was read of the account's images.

ImageKeys.description: The image keys `key image` derived from the `kvcomm` cache and checked against the account's images.

CandidateSource.description: A `kvcomm` file a code was read from, and how its name was read.

result.description: The helper's answer; `{"raw": …}` when it is not JSON.

ScannedImageKeys.description: What `key scan-image` (macOS) answers: the helper's own result.

BackupManifest.description: What a backup holds (`backup inspect`): the manifest stored in the archive.

path.description: Its path in the backup: `db_storage/…`, `FileStorage/…` or `emojis/…`.

DbCandidates.description: The default places of WeChat's data directory (`db detect`).

DbCandidate.description: A place WeChat's data directory may be.

DbAccounts.description: The accounts in WeChat's data directory (`db wxid`).

wxid.description: As `config set wxid` takes it, without the suffix of its folder's name.

DbAccount.description: An account of WeChat's data directory.

DbConnection.description: That the databases open with the configured key (`db test`); a failure is an error instead.

private_sessions.description: The private chats with a message in the range, the latest first.

private_segments.description: The stretches of each private chat, in time order: a new one begins after a long pause.

mentions.description: The group messages that @-mention me, the latest first.

mention_groups.description: The groups of those, the one with the most first.

Footprint.description:
My footprint over a range of days (`insight footprint`): who I talked with and replied to, and where I was
@-mentioned. Its keys are the native layer's, in snake_case. Times are Unix seconds, 0 where there is none.

private_inbound_people.description: The people who wrote to me.

anchor_local_id.description: The message to open the chat at, by its local id and time.

FootprintSession.description: A private chat of the footprint.

FootprintSegment.description: A stretch of a private chat.

source.description: The message's `source` XML, which lists who it mentions.

truncated.description: Whether a list was cut at its limit.

data.description: By username, in the order asked for.

ExportStats.description: What the export window shows of each conversation asked for (`chat export-stats`).

groupMyMessages.description: A group's: my messages in it.

groupActiveSpeakers.description: A group's: the members who said something.

groupMutualFriends.description: A group's, with relations: its members who are my friends.

privateMutualGroups.description: A private chat's, with relations: the groups we are both in.

SessionExportStats.description: One conversation's messages by type, within the range asked for, and its relations.

TransferNames.description: The names a group's transfer message shows for its two sides (`chat transfer-names`).

InsightLookup.description:
One insight record (`insight get`), with `success` inside as the desktop app has it. A record not found is a
failure of the command instead, so an answer that succeeds holds `success: true` and the record.

InsightRecord.description: An insight the engine wrote about a conversation.

InsightRecordLog.description: What was asked of the AI model for a record, and what it answered.

success.description: Always true: the desktop app's shape.

contacts.description: Everyone with a record, the most records first.

InsightRecords.description: A page of the account's insight records (`insight records`), the newest first, with counts over all of them.

InsightSummary.description: An insight record as lists and events name it, without its log.

InsightTodayStat.description: How often the engine wrote about a conversation today (`insight today-stats`).

InsightMarked.description: What `insight mark-read` answers; a record not found is a failure of the command.

InsightScan.description: What `insight scan` answers: the insights the silence scan wrote.

message.description: What happened, in the server's language.

InsightReply.description:
What `insight test`, `trigger` and `footprint-summary` answer; when the AI is not set up or answers nothing, the
command fails with `message` instead.

command.description: The command line it runs, `weflow` first (`weflow --json --progress export messages …`).

httpStatus.description: The status a synchronous request would have got.

file.description: The file of a job started with `return=file`, once it has succeeded: `GET /jobs/{id}/file`.

Job.description:
A job as `/jobs` answers it (`Prefer: respond-async`, #398): the command it runs, how far it is and how it ended.
Times are Unix milliseconds.

Error.description:
What went wrong (`error` of a failed answer): `code` names the kind of failure, `message` says it for a person,
`details` adds what some codes have to say.

Row.description: A row of one of WeChat's tables, with its columns; not described further, as WeChat decides them
